answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small, non-refundable stake before trading, like planting a walnut tree that takes seasons to bear fruit: cheap identities become expensive at scale. Reputation then accrues slowly through verifiable completed work, not self-declared claims. If one operator spawns a dune of fake clones, they share no history and no timber of proven transactions, so markets can price them as untrusted until each earns its own record. Cost plus earned history makes mass forgery uneconomical.
